current_workflow.step: A requester emails the desk a free-form request for a new deal ticket. Counterparty, meter, volume and pricing appear in whatever layout the sender chooses, and sometimes there is only a one-line ask with no details.
current_workflow.who: producer services / field origination (e.g. Vance Taylor, Susan Smith), Volume Management

current_workflow.step: For multi-party transactions such as storage purchases, one email asks several desks to enter matching Sitara deals on the same day, and asks treasury to wire payment.

Change requests (zero out expected volume, cut off a deal going forward, change pricing, kill rather than zero) reach the desk by email or phone. Each one cites deal numbers from an earlier list or thread.
current_workflow.who: Volume Management, storage, accounting, Unify support

current_workflow.step: The desk scheduler enters or edits the ticket in Sitara. Transport usage tickets are refreshed in bulk, and schedulers are then asked to check that volumes show correctly in Position Manager.
No standard confirmation goes back, so requesters follow up to find out whether the deal is in, priced or pathed. Around month start, unpathed and unassigned deals get escalated to supervisors.
Months later, accounting asks why historic deals were changed or suspended. The reason was never recorded with the request, so the trail has to be rebuilt by asking around.

implementation_steps: Collect a sample of past requests (field origination, storage, Volume Management, accounting) and confirm which fields the desk had to chase. Finalize the template field list with Daren Farmer and Pat Clynes.

Write the template with a fixed subject tag (for example 'SITARA REQ: <action> <counterparty>') and the guidance on zeroing out instead of killing deals, reviewed with Unify support (Tammy Jaquet) and Volume Management (Rita Wynne).
Write the prepared confirmation reply and the incomplete-request reply. Save both as stationery/saved replies in the desk schedulers' mail clients.
Write the month-start checklist: list unpathed deals per pipe, confirm the scheduler assigned to each pipe, and list open template requests due for the coming close.

Send the template to the regular requesters (field origination, storage book, Volume Management, accounting) with a short note. From then on, the desk replies to any free-form request with the template attached and asks for it to be resent.
Run the checklist at the next month start. Pat Clynes reviews it and assigns any pipe without an owner.
After one close, count requests that needed a follow-up or clarification round and adjust the fields.
risks: Requesters keep sending free-form emails or phoning changes in. To counter this, the desk consistently replies with the template, and supervisors back the rule for EOL and after-hours changes.

The evidence does not show how many requests are actually incomplete compared with simply waiting in a queue. If most delay is desk capacity, the template removes fewer rounds than expected, so measure follow-ups before and after.
The field list rests on a 15-message sample. Some request types (transport usage tickets, multi-party storage deals) may need extra fields, so review the template after the first close.
Confirmation replies add a small amount of desk work per request. Keep the reply short and prefilled so it costs less than the follow-up emails it replaces.
The value is small (about $65 per month), so the rollout should stay low-cost and avoid any system build.

solution.approach: Publish one 'Sitara Deal Request' email template. Every requester copies it into new requests to the logistics desk. Its fixed fields are: action (create / change price / change volume / zero out / cut off / path), existing Sitara deal number(s) if any, counterparty, meter, pipe, start and end dates, daily volume, price or index formula, book, contract in place (Y/N), close month needed by, and reason for the change. A short guidance block in the template tells requesters to zero out deals instead of killing them when paths exist, because killed deals break Unify paths. It also tells them that phoned-in or EOL changes must be confirmed by email using the template. The desk answers each request with a prepared confirmation reply: Sitara number(s) created or changed, the fields as entered, the date entered, and whether Position Manager and pathing were checked. This reply closes the loop and gives accounting a written reason for later audits. A one-page month-start checklist covers the cases that currently escalate: unpathed deals by pipe, owner for each pipe, and open template requests with a close-month deadline.
components: Sitara Deal Request email template (fixed fields plus zero-out-not-kill guidance)
prepared confirmation reply for the desk returning the Sitara number
short 'incomplete request' reply that lists the missing fields
shared mailbox folder or rule that files template requests by subject tag
inputs: requester's filled-in Sitara Deal Request template
existing Sitara deal numbers and tickets
pipe-to-scheduler assignment list for the month
outputs: confirmation reply to the requester with the Sitara number(s) and fields as entered
written reason for each change kept in the email thread for accounting
month-start checklist of unpathed deals and owners for the logistics supervisor
solution.trigger: An incoming email asking the logistics desk to create or change a Sitara deal, plus the month-start/close deadline for the checklist.

stays_manual: Actual entry and editing of deals in Sitara. The desk still keys tickets and judges pricing and contract coverage.
Deciding whether a deal should be killed or zeroed out when Unify paths exist, which needs the scheduler's view of the paths.
Assigning pipe ownership when schedulers change, which is a supervisor decision.
Research on historic or suspended deals for accounting. The template only helps for requests made after rollout.
success_metric: Share of Sitara deal requests to the logistics desk that receive a follow-up or 'have you had a chance' email before confirmation, plus the count of deals found unpathed at month start, compared before and after rollout.
summary: Traders, field-services staff, storage and accounting email the logistics desk (mainly Daren Farmer) free-form requests to create, zero out, cut off, re-price or path Sitara deals. These requests often lack key fields, have no stated close deadline and never get a deal-number confirmation back, so requesters chase them for days. The fix is a standard Sitara deal request template, a matching confirmation reply that returns the Sitara number, and a short pre-close checklist. Together they remove the clarification and follow-up rounds (estimated at $65 per month, $780 per year, at $85 per hour).
